大中中，朱邪執宜為刺史

以兄嗣本為振武節度使

units.en: Geography Treatise V — Western Capital (Xijing) Circuit
units.literal: Geography Treatise V: Western Capital Circuit

units.zh: 西京大同府，陶唐冀州之域。
units.en: Datong Prefecture at the Western Capital was ancient Ji territory under Yao.
units.literal: Western Capital Datong Prefecture—the land of Ji in Yao's era.

units.en: Shun assigned it to Bing Province.
units.literal: In Shun's time it was allotted to Bing Province.

units.en: Under Xia it returned to Ji Province.
units.literal: Under Xia it again belonged to Ji Province.

units.en: The Zhou Offices of Region name the north Bing Province.
units.literal: The Zhou Offices of Region call the due north Bing Province.

units.zh: 戰國屬趙，武靈王始置雲中郡。
units.en: In the Warring States era it lay in Zhao; King Wuling of Zhao first created Yunzhong Commandery.
units.literal: In the Warring States it belonged to Zhao; King Wuling first established Yunzhong Commandery.

units.zh: 秦屬代王國，後為平城縣。
units.en: Qin placed it in the princely kingdom of Dai; later it was Pingcheng County.
units.literal: Under Qin it belonged to the Dai princely kingdom; later it became Pingcheng County.

units.en: Under Wei it fell within Xinxing Commandery.
units.literal: Under Wei it belonged to Xinxing Commandery.

units.en: Under Jin it remained in Yanmen.
units.literal: Jin still assigned it to Yanmen.

units.zh: 劉琨表封猗盧為代王，都平城。
units.en: Liu Kun petitioned to enfeoff Yilu as Prince of Dai with his seat at Pingcheng.
units.literal: Liu Kun memorialized to enfeoff Yilu as Prince of Dai, with capital at Pingcheng.

units.zh: 元魏道武於此遂建都邑。
units.en: Northern Wei's Emperor Daowu founded his capital here.
units.literal: Northern Wei Emperor Daowu hereupon founded his capital seat.

units.zh: 孝文帝改為司州牧，置代尹，遷都洛邑，改萬年，又置恒州。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowen made it Sizhou pastoral domain, appointed a Dai intendant, relocated the capital to Luoyang, renamed the seat Wannian, and added Heng Prefecture.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowen changed it to Sizhou pastoral supervisor, set a Dai intendant, moved the capital to Luoyang, renamed it Wannian, and also established Heng Prefecture.

units.zh: 高齊文宣帝廢州為恒安鎮，今謂之東城，尋復恒州。
units.en: Northern Qi Emperor Wenxuan reduced the prefecture to Heng'an Fort—today's Eastern City—then restored Heng Prefecture.
units.literal: Northern Qi Emperor Wenxuan abolished the prefecture for Heng'an Fort; today this is called the Eastern City; soon Heng Prefecture was restored.

units.en: Zhou reinstated Heng'an Fort as Shuo Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhou again made Heng'an Fort and changed the name to Shuo Prefecture.

units.en: Under Sui it remained a fortified post.
units.literal: Sui still kept it as a fort.

units.zh: 唐武德四年置北恒州，七年廢。
units.en: Tang Wude year 4 set up Northern Heng Prefecture; in year 7 it was abolished.
units.literal: Tang year 4 of Wude established Northern Heng Prefecture; year 7 it was abolished.

units.zh: 貞觀十四年，移雲中定襄縣於此。
units.en: In Zhenguan year 14 Dingxiang County from Yunzhong was moved here.
units.literal: Zhenguan year 14 moved Yunzhong's Dingxiang County here.

units.zh: 永淳元年，默啜為民患，移民朔州。
units.en: In the first year of Yongchun, Mochuo's raids harried the people, and the populace was relocated to Shuo.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, Mochuo troubled the people; populations were moved to Shuo Prefecture.

units.en: Kaiyuan year 18 created Yun Prefecture.
units.literal: Kaiyuan year 18 established Yun Prefecture.

units.en: In the first year of Tianbao it became Yunzhong Commandery.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianbao changed it to Yunzhong Commandery.

units.en: In the first year of Qianyuan it reverted to the name Yun Prefecture.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan it was called Yun Prefecture.

units.zh: 乾符三年，大同軍節度使李國昌子克用為雲中守捉使，殺防禦使，據州以聞。
units.en: In Qianfu year 3 Li Guochang, Datong Army military commissioner, had a son Keyong who served as Yunzhong defense commissioner; Keyong slew the defense envoy, seized the prefecture, and sent word to court.
units.literal: Qianfu year 3, Datong Army military commissioner Li Guochang's son Keyong served as Yunzhong defense commissioner, killed the defense envoy, held the prefecture and reported to the throne.

units.zh: 僖宗赦克用，以國昌為大同軍防禦使，不受命。
units.en: Emperor Xizong amnestied Keyong and appointed Guochang Datong Army defense envoy, but Guochang refused the order.
units.literal: Emperor Xizong pardoned Keyong, making Guochang Datong Army defense envoy; he did not accept the appointment.

units.zh: 廣明元年，李琢攻國昌，國昌兵敗，與克用奔北地。
units.en: In the first year of Guangming Li Zhuo struck Guochang; defeated, Guochang fled north with Keyong.
units.literal: In the first year of Guangming, Li Zhuo attacked Guochang; Guochang's army was defeated and with Keyong fled to the Northern Land.

units.zh: 黃巢入京師，詔發代北軍，尋赦國昌，使討賊。
units.en: When Huang Chao took the capital, court ordered the Dai-north armies mobilized and soon pardoned Guochang to campaign against the rebels.
units.literal: Huang Chao entered the capital; an edict raised the Dai-north armies; soon Guochang was pardoned and ordered to attack the rebels.

units.zh: 克用率三萬五千騎而南，收京師功第一，國昌封隴西郡王。
units.en: Keyong marched south with thirty-five thousand horsemen; his service in retaking the capital ranked first, and Guochang was made Prince of Longxi Commandery.
units.literal: Keyong led thirty-five thousand cavalry south; in recovering the capital his merit ranked first; Guochang was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi Commandery.

units.en: After Guochang died, Keyong seized Yun Prefecture.
units.literal: Guochang died; Keyong took Yun Prefecture.

units.zh: 既而所向失利，乃卑詞厚禮，與太祖會於雲州之東城，謀大舉兵攻梁，不果。
units.en: When his campaigns faltered, Keyong sent humble envoys and lavish gifts to meet the Taizu at Yun Prefecture's Eastern City and plot a major strike against Liang—but the plan never materialized.
units.literal: Soon afterward his campaigns met reverses; he then sent humble words and rich gifts and met the Taizu at Yun Prefecture's Eastern City to plan a great attack on Liang, but it did not come to pass.

units.zh: 克用子存勖滅梁，是為唐莊宗。
units.en: Keyong's son Cunxu overthrew Liang and became Tang Emperor Zhuangzong.
units.literal: Keyong's son Cunxu destroyed Liang; this was Tang Emperor Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 同光三年，復以雲州為大同軍節度使。
units.en: In Tongguang year 3 Yun Prefecture was again the headquarters of the Datong Army command.
units.literal: Tongguang year 3 again made Yun Prefecture the seat of the Datong Army military commissioner.

units.zh: 晉高祖代唐，以契丹有援立功，割山前、代北地為賂，大同來屬，因建西京。
units.en: When Jin Gaozu supplanted Tang he rewarded Khitan aid by ceding the mountain-front and northern Dai territories; Datong passed to Liao and the Western Capital was founded.
units.literal: Jin Emperor Gaozu replaced Tang; because the Khitan had aided him and won merit, he ceded the lands south of the mountains and north of Dai as tribute; Datong came under Liao rule and the Western Capital was established.

units.en: Watchtowers and stockades were fully built.
units.literal: Enemy towers and palisades were complete.

units.en: The city measured twenty li on each side.
units.literal: Twenty li in length and breadth.

units.zh: 門，東曰迎春，南曰朝陽，西曰定西，北曰拱極。
units.en: Its gates were Yingchun to the east, Chaoyang to the south, Dingxi to the west, and Gongji to the north.
units.literal: Gates: east called Yingchun, south Chaoyang, west Dingxi, north Gongji.

units.zh: 元魏宮垣占城之北面，雙闕尚在。
units.en: Northern Wei palace ramparts took up the north side of the city; the paired gate towers remain.
units.literal: Northern Wei palace walls occupied the city's north face; paired gate towers still stand.

units.zh: 遼既建都，用為重地，非親王不得主之。
units.en: After Liao made this a capital seat it became a place of high importance—only princes of the blood could hold it.
units.literal: Once Liao had established its capital here it was treated as a weighty post; none but imperial princes might govern it.

units.zh: 清寧八年建華巖寺，奉安諸帝石像、銅像。
units.en: Qingning year 8 saw Huayan Temple erected to house stone and bronze imperial images.
units.literal: In Qingning year 8 Huayan Temple was built to enshrine stone and bronze images of the emperors.

units.zh: 又有天王寺、留守司衙，南曰西省。
units.en: The city also held Tianwang Temple and the resident commissioner's yamen; the southern quarter was called the Western Secretariat.
units.literal: There were also Tianwang Temple and the headquarters of the resident commissioner; to the south was called the Western Secretariat.

units.zh: 北門之東曰大同府，北門之西曰大同驛。
units.en: East of the North Gate lay Datong Prefecture; west of it lay Datong Post Station.
units.literal: East of the north gate was Datong Prefecture; west of the north gate was Datong Post Station.

units.zh: 初為大同軍節度，重熙十三年升為西京，府曰大同。
units.en: It began as the Datong Army headquarters; in Chongxi year 13 it was promoted to Western Capital with Datong as the prefectural seat.
units.literal: At first it was the Datong Army command; in Chongxi year 13 it was raised to the Western Capital, the prefecture called Datong.

units.en: It administered two sub-prefectures and seven counties:
units.literal: It governed two prefectures and seven counties:

units.en: Datong County.
units.literal: Datong County.

units.en: It was originally the Datong River valley.
units.literal: Originally the land of Datong River valley.

units.zh: 重熙十七年西夏犯邊，析雲中縣置。
units.en: Chongxi year 17, after a Western Xia border raid, it was carved from Yunzhong County.
units.literal: In Chongxi year 17 when Western Xia raided the border, it was split off from Yunzhong County and established.

units.en: Ten thousand registered households.
units.literal: Ten thousand households.

units.en: Yunzhong County.
units.literal: Yunzhong County.

units.en: Zhao founded it.
units.literal: Established by Zhao.

units.en: Its administrative history follows that of the capital seat.
units.literal: Its administrative history matches that of the capital prefecture.

units.en: Ten thousand registered households.
units.literal: Ten thousand households.

units.en: Tiancheng County.
units.literal: Tiancheng County.

units.en: It was originally the outermost frontier territory.
units.literal: Originally the outermost frontier land.

units.zh: 魏道武帝置廣牧縣，唐武德五年置定襄縣，遼析雲中置。
units.en: Northern Wei Daowu created Guangmu County; Tang Wude year 5 added Dingxiang County; Liao carved it from Yunzhong.
units.literal: Northern Wei Emperor Daowu set Guangmu County; Tang Wude year 5 set Dingxiang County; Liao split it from Yunzhong.

units.en: It lay one hundred eighty li north of the capital.
units.literal: One hundred eighty li north of the capital.

units.en: Five thousand registered households.
units.literal: Five thousand households.

units.en: Yu Prefecture—Zhongshun Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.
units.literal: Yu Prefecture, Zhongshun Army, upper grade, military commissioner.

units.zh: 《周職方》，并州川曰漚夷，在州境飛狐縣。
units.en: The Zhou Offices of the Realm names Bing Province's river Ouyi, located in Feihu County within this prefecture.
units.literal: The Zhou "Offices of the Realm" records that Bing Province's river was called Ouyi, in Feihu County within the prefecture.

units.zh: 趙襄子滅代，武靈王置代郡；
units.en: Zhao Xiangzi destroyed Dai; King Wuling of Zhao founded Dai Commandery;
units.literal: Zhao Xiangzi destroyed Dai; King Wuling of Zhao established Dai Commandery;

units.zh: 項羽徙趙歇為代王，歇還趙，立陳余王代；
units.en: Xiang Yu installed Zhao Xie as king of Dai; Xie returned to Zhao and Chen Yu was enthroned as king of Dai;
units.literal: Xiang Yu moved Zhao Xie to be king of Dai; Xie returned to Zhao and Chen Yu was made king of Dai;

units.en: Han Xin of Han killed Yu and re-established Dai Commandery;
units.literal: Han's Han Xin slew Yu and restored Dai Commandery;

units.en: Emperor Wen first enfeoffed Dai here;
units.literal: Emperor Wen at first enfeoffed Dai here;

units.en: all these events took place here.
units.literal: all these events concern this place.

units.zh: 周宣帝始置蔚州，隋開皇中廢。
units.en: Emperor Xuan of Zhou first founded Yu Prefecture; Sui Kaihuang abolished it.
units.literal: Emperor Xuan of Zhou first established Yu Prefecture; Sui Kaihuang abolished it.

units.en: Tang Wude year 4 re-established it.
units.literal: Tang Wude year 4 restored it.

units.en: Zhide year 2 it was renamed Xingtang County.
units.literal: Zhide year 2 changed it to Xingtang County.

units.en: Qianyuan year 1 it reverted to the former arrangement.
units.literal: Qianyuan year 1 restored the former name.

units.zh: 大中中，朱邪執宜為刺史，有功，賜姓名李國昌。
units.en: In the Dazhong era Zhuye Zhiyi was prefect; for his service he was granted the surname and name Li Guochang.
units.literal: In the Dazhong era Zhuye Zhiyi served as prefect, merited reward, and was granted the surname and personal name Li Guochang.

units.zh: 子克用乞為留後，僖宗不許。
units.en: His son Keyong asked to stay on as acting commissioner; Emperor Xizong refused.
units.literal: His son Keyong petitioned to remain as acting commissioner; Emperor Xizong refused.

units.zh: 廣明初，攻敗國昌，代北無備，太祖來攻，克之，俘掠居民而去。
units.en: Early in the Guangming era, Guochang was defeated in an attack; with northern Dai undefended, Taizu attacked, took it, and carried off the populace.
units.literal: Early in the Guangming era, Guochang was defeated in an attack; northern Dai was undefended; Taizu came, seized it, and carried off the inhabitants.

units.zh: 石晉獻地，升忠順軍，後更武安軍。
units.en: Later Jin surrendered the territory; it was promoted to Zhongshun Army and later renamed Wu'an Army.
units.literal: Later Jin ceded the territory; it was raised to Zhongshun Army, later changed to Wu'an Army.

units.zh: 統和四年入宋，尋復之，降刺史，隸奉聖州，升觀察，復忠順軍節度。
units.en: Tonghe year 4 it briefly fell to Song but was soon recovered; it was reduced to a prefect, placed under Fengsheng Prefecture, raised to surveillance commissioner, and restored as Zhongshun Army command.
units.literal: Tonghe year 4 it fell to Song, was soon recovered, reduced to a prefect, subordinated to Fengsheng Prefecture, raised to surveillance commissioner, and restored as Zhongshun Army command.

units.en: Its military affairs came under the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.
units.literal: Military affairs belonged to the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.

units.en: The prefecture administered five counties: Lingxian County.
units.literal: It governed five counties: Lingxian County.

units.zh: 唐置興唐縣，梁改隆化縣，後唐同光初復置，晉改今名。
units.en: Tang founded Xingtang County; Liang renamed it Longhua County; early Later Tang Tongguang restored it; Jin gave it the present name.
units.literal: Tang established Xingtang County; Liang changed it to Longhua County; early Later Tang Tongguang restored it; Jin changed to the present name.

units.en: Twenty thousand registered households.
units.literal: Twenty thousand households.

units.en: Changqing County.
units.literal: Changqing County.

units.en: It was originally Baideng Platform.
units.literal: Originally the land of Baideng Platform.

units.zh: 冒頓單于縱精騎三十餘萬圍漢高帝於白登七日，即此。
units.en: Here the Xiongnu chanyu Modu with over three hundred thousand picked horsemen besieged Han Emperor Gaodi at Baideng for seven days.
units.literal: The Xiongnu chanyu Modu with more than three hundred thousand elite cavalry besieged Han Emperor Gaodi at Baideng for seven days—this was the place.

units.en: Liao first created the county.
units.literal: Liao first established the county.

units.en: The Qingpo marsh lies there.
units.literal: There is Qingpo.

units.zh: 梁元帝《橫吹曲》云「朝跋青陂，暮上白登。」
units.en: Liang Emperor Yuan's Hengchui lyric runs: "At dawn we ford Qingpo; at dusk we climb Baideng."
units.literal: Liang Emperor Yuan's Hengchui song says: "At dawn we ford Qingpo; at dusk we climb Baideng."

units.en: It stood one hundred ten li north of Eastern Capital.
units.literal: It lies one hundred ten li north of Eastern Capital.

units.en: Four thousand registered households.
units.literal: Four thousand households.

units.en: Fengyi County.
units.literal: Fengyi County.

units.en: It was originally Han Taolin County.
units.literal: Originally Han Taolin County land.

units.en: Later Tang's Emperor Wu met the Taizu here.
units.literal: Later Tang Emperor Wu met the Taizu here.

units.en: Liao carved it from Yunzhong County.
units.literal: Liao split it from Yunzhong.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Feng Prefecture—Tiande Army, with a military commissioner.
units.literal: Feng Prefecture, Tiande Army, jiedushi.

units.zh: 秦為上郡北境，漢屬五原郡。
units.en: In Qin it formed the northern frontier of Shang Commandery; under Han it lay in Wuyuan Commandery.
units.literal: In Qin it was the northern border of Shang Commandery; in Han it belonged to Wuyuan Commandery.

units.en: The soil was salty and barren, with scant farmland.
units.literal: The land is saline and alkaline, with little arable fields.

units.zh: 自晉永嘉之亂，屬赫連勃勃。
units.en: After Jin's Yongjia upheaval it fell under Helian Bobo.
units.literal: Since the Yongjia turmoil of Jin, it belonged to Helian Bobo.

units.en: Later Zhou set up Yongfeng Fort.
units.literal: Later Zhou established Yongfeng Fort.

units.zh: 隋開皇中升永豐縣，改豐州。
units.en: In Sui Kaihuang it was promoted to Yongfeng County and renamed Feng Prefecture.
units.literal: Sui Kaihuang era raised it to Yongfeng County and changed it to Feng Prefecture.

units.zh: 大業七年為五原郡，義寧元年，太守張遜奏改歸順郡。
units.en: Daye year 7 made it Wuyuan Commandery; Yining year 1 Prefect Zhang Xun petitioned to rename it Guishun Commandery.
units.literal: Daye year 7 it became Wuyuan Commandery; in the first year of Yining, Administrator Zhang Xun memorialized to change it to Guishun Commandery.

units.zh: 唐武德元年為豐州總管府。
units.en: In Tang Wude year 1 it became the Feng Prefecture grand commandant headquarters.
units.literal: Tang Wude year 1 it became Feng Prefecture grand commandant headquarters.

units.zh: 六年省，遷民於白馬縣，遂廢。
units.en: In year 6 the prefecture was removed, the populace relocated to Baima County, and it was abandoned.
units.literal: Year 6 it was abolished; populations were moved to Baima County, and it was then abandoned.

units.zh: 貞觀四年分靈州境，置相州都督府，領蕃戶。
units.en: Zhenguan year 4 carved territory from Ling Prefecture, set up Xiang Prefecture grand commandant headquarters, and administered frontier households.
units.literal: Zhenguan year 4 split off Ling Prefecture territory, established Xiang Prefecture grand commandant headquarters, governing frontier households.

units.en: Early Tianbao it became Jiuyuan Commandery.
units.literal: Early Tianbao changed it to Jiuyuan Commandery.

units.zh: 乾元元年復豐州，後入回鶻。
units.en: Qianyuan year 1 Feng Prefecture was restored; later it passed to the Uighurs.
units.literal: Qianyuan year 1 restored Feng Prefecture; later it fell to the Uighurs.

units.zh: 會昌中克之，後唐改天德軍。
units.en: The Huichang period retook it; Later Tang renamed it Tiande Army.
units.literal: Huichang era recaptured it; Later Tang changed it to Tiande Army.

units.zh: 太祖神冊五年攻下，更名應天軍，復為州。
units.en: Taizu year 5 of Shence seized it, renamed it Yingtian Army, and restored it as a prefecture.
units.literal: In year 5 of Emperor Taizu's Shence reign it was stormed, renamed Yingtian Army, then restored as a prefecture.

units.zh: 有大鹽濼、九十九泉、沒越濼、古磧口、青冢，即王昭君墓，兵事屬西南面招討司。
units.en: It has Great Salt Marsh, Ninety-Nine Springs, Moyue Marsh, ancient Qikou Pass, and Qingzhong, Wang Zhaojun's tomb; military affairs came under the Southwest Pacification Office.
units.literal: There are Great Salt Marsh, Ninety-Nine Springs, Moyue Marsh, ancient Qikou Pass, and Qingzhong—the tomb of Wang Zhaojun; military affairs belonged to the Southwest Pacification Office.

units.en: The prefecture administered two counties: Fumin County.
units.literal: It governed two counties: Fumin County.

units.en: It was Han Linrong County; Liao gave it the present name.
units.literal: Originally Han Linrong County; Liao changed to the present name.

units.en: 1,200 registered households.
units.literal: One thousand two hundred households.

units.en: Huairen County.
units.literal: Huairen County.

units.en: It was originally Han Shanan County.
units.literal: Originally Han Shanan County.

units.en: During Northern Wei Ge Rong's revolt the county was abandoned.
units.literal: Northern Wei Ge Rong's rebellion; the county was abolished.

units.zh: 隋開皇二年移雲內於此。
units.en: Sui Kaihuang year 2 relocated Yunnei here.
units.literal: Sui Kaihuang year 2 moved Yunnei here.

units.zh: 大業二年置大利縣，屬雲州，改屬定襄郡。
units.en: Daye year 2 created Dali County under Yun Prefecture, later reassigned to Dingxiang Commandery.
units.literal: Daye year 2 established Dali County, belonging to Yun Prefecture; later it was changed to Dingxiang Commandery.

units.en: In late Sui it was lost to the Turks.
units.literal: At the end of Sui it fell to the Turks.

units.zh: 李克用敗赫連鐸，駐兵於此。
units.en: Li Keyong defeated Helian Duo and stationed troops here.
units.literal: Li Keyong defeated Helian Duo and encamped here.

units.en: Liao renamed it Huairen.
units.literal: Liao changed the name to Huairen.

units.en: It lay sixty li south of the capital.
units.literal: Sixty li south of the capital.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Huai'an County.
units.literal: Huai'an County.

units.en: It was originally Han Yiyu County.
units.literal: Originally Han Yiyu County land.

units.zh: 歷魏至隋，為突厥所據，唐克頡利，縣遂廢為懷荒鎮。
units.en: From Wei through Sui Turks held it; after Tang defeated Jieli the county was abolished and became Huaihuang Fort.
units.literal: From Wei through Sui it was held by the Turks; Tang conquered Jieli and the county was abolished for Huaihuang Fort.

units.zh: 高勛鎮燕，奏分歸化州文德縣置。
units.en: Under Gao Xun's rule in Yan he petitioned to carve Wende County from Guihua Prefecture and establish this county.
units.literal: When Gao Xun governed Yan he memorialized to split off Wende County of Guihua Prefecture and establish this.

units.en: Initially it answered to Fengsheng Prefecture; later it was transferred here.
units.literal: At first it was subordinate to Fengsheng Prefecture; later it came under this circuit.

units.en: It stood two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.
units.literal: Two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Hong Prefecture—Boning Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Hong Prefecture, Boling Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Eastern Wei Emperor Jing founded Northern Lingqiu County.
units.literal: Eastern Wei Emperor Jing established Northern Lingqiu County.

units.zh: 唐初地陷突厥，開元中置橫野軍安邊縣，天寶亂廢，後為襄陰村。
units.en: Early Tang lost the region to Turks; Kaiyuan saw Hengye Army and Anbian County, abolished in the Tianbao disorders; later it became Xiangyin village.
units.literal: Early Tang the land fell to the Turks; in Kaiyuan a Hengye Army and Anbian County were set up; abolished in the Tianbao turmoil; later it was Xiangyin village.

units.zh: 統和中，以寰州近邊，為宋將潘美所破，廢之，乃於此置弘州，初軍曰永寧。
units.en: During Tonghe, after border prefecture Huan was smashed by Song general Pan Mei and abolished, Hong Prefecture was founded here; its army was first called Yongning.
units.literal: In Tonghe, because Huan Prefecture lay on the border and was broken by Song general Pan Mei, it was abolished and Hong Prefecture was established here; at first the army was called Yongning.

units.zh: 有桑乾河、白道泉、白登山，亦曰火燒山，有火井。
units.en: It has the Sanggan River, Baidao Spring, Mount Baideng (also Mount Huoshao), and a fire well.
units.literal: There are the Sanggan River, Baidao Spring, Mount Baideng—also called Mount Huoshao—and a fire well.

units.en: It administered two counties:
units.literal: It governed two counties:

units.en: Yongning County.
units.literal: Yongning County.

units.en: Ten thousand registered households.
units.literal: Ten thousand households.

units.en: Shunsheng County.
units.literal: Shunsheng County.

units.en: It was Northern Wei's Anse Army, abandoned amid Five Dynasties fighting.
units.literal: Originally Northern Wei Anse Army; abolished in Five Dynasties warfare.

units.zh: 高勛鎮幽州，奏景宗分永興縣置。
units.en: Under Gao Xun in Youzhou he petitioned Emperor Jingzong to carve Yongxing County and establish this county.
units.literal: When Gao Xun governed Youzhou he memorialized for Emperor Jingzong to split off Yongxing County and establish this.

units.en: It initially answered to Fengsheng Prefecture.
units.literal: At first subordinate to Fengsheng Prefecture.

units.en: It stood two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.
units.literal: Two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: De Prefecture, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: De Prefecture, lower grade, cishi.

units.zh: 唐會昌中以西德店置德州。
units.en: In Tang's Huichang period De Prefecture was set up at Xide post.
units.literal: Tang Huichang era established De Prefecture at Xide post.

units.en: Kaitai year 8 it was re-established for Han settlers.
units.literal: Kaitai year 8 restored it with Han households.

units.zh: 有步落泉、金河山、野狐嶺、白道阪。
units.en: It has Buluo Spring, Jinhe Mountain, Yehu Ridge, and Baidao Slope.
units.literal: There are Buluo Spring, Jinhe Mountain, Yehu Ridge, and Baidao Slope.

units.en: One county:
units.literal: One county:

units.en: Xuande County.
units.literal: Xuande County.

units.zh: 本漢桐過縣地，屬雲中郡，後隸定襄郡，漢末廢。
units.en: It was Han Tongguo County in Yunzhong Commandery, later in Dingxiang Commandery, abandoned in late Han.
units.literal: Originally Han Tongguo County land, belonging to Yunzhong Commandery; later subordinate to Dingxiang Commandery; abolished at the end of Han.

units.en: Northern Qi established Zi'a Fort.
units.literal: Northern Qi set Zi'a Fort.

units.en: Tang's Huichang period created the county.
units.literal: Tang Huichang era established the county.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Zhenwu County.
units.literal: Zhenwu County.

units.en: It was Han Dingxiang Commandery's Shengle County.
units.literal: Originally Han Dingxiang Commandery Shengle County.

units.en: It lay against the Yin Mountains with the Yellow River before it.
units.literal: Backed by the Yin Mountains, fronting the Yellow River.

units.en: Northern Wei once held its capital at Shengle—here.
units.literal: Northern Wei once made Shengle its capital—this was the place.

units.zh: 唐武德四年克突厥，建雲中都督府。
units.en: Tang Wude year 4, after defeating the Turks, established the Yunzhong area command.
units.literal: Tang Wude year 4 conquered the Turks and built the Yunzhong area command.

units.zh: 麟德三年改單于大都督府。
units.en: Linde year 3 it became the Chanyu grand area command.
units.literal: Linde year 3 changed it to the Chanyu grand area command.

units.zh: 聖歷元年又改安北都督。
units.en: In the first year of Shengli it was renamed the Anbei area command.
units.literal: In the first year of Shengli again changed it to the Anbei area command.

units.zh: 開元七年割隸東受降城。
units.en: Kaiyuan year 7 it was detached and placed under Eastern Shouxiang Fort.
units.literal: Kaiyuan year 7 cut off and subordinated to Eastern Shouxiang Fort.

units.en: Year 8 created the Zhenwu Army command.
units.literal: Year 8 established the Zhenwu Army military commissioner.

units.zh: 會昌五年為安北都護府。
units.en: In Huichang year 5 the seat was raised to the Anbei grand protectorate.
units.literal: Huichang year 5 it became the Anbei grand protectorate.

units.zh: 後唐莊宗以兄嗣本為振武節度使。
units.en: Later Tang Zhuangzong made his elder brother Siben military commissioner of Zhenwu.
units.literal: Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong appointed his elder brother Siben Zhenwu military commissioner.

units.zh: 太祖神冊元年，伐吐渾還，攻之，盡俘其民以東，唯存鄉兵三百人防戍。
units.en: In the Taizu's first year of divine enthronement, returning from a Tuyuhun campaign, he attacked the place, deported the entire population eastward, and left only three hundred local militia on guard.
units.literal: In the first year of Taizu of divine enthronement, returning from campaigning against the Tuyuhun, attacked it and took all its people east; only three hundred local militia remained to garrison.

units.en: Later it was restored as a county.
units.literal: Later it was again made a county.

units.en: Yunnei Prefecture—Kaiyuan Army, lower grade, with a military commissioner.
units.literal: Yunnei Prefecture, Kaiyuan Army, lower grade, military commissioner.

units.en: It was originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.
units.literal: Originally Middle Shouxiang Fort land.

units.zh: 遼初置代北雲朔招討司，改雲內州。
units.en: Early Liao placed the Dai-north Yun-Shuo pacification office here, later renamed Yunnei Prefecture.
units.literal: At the founding of Liao the Dai-north Yun-Shuo pacification office was set up; changed to Yunnei Prefecture.

units.en: It was raised in rank at the start of Qingning.
units.literal: Early Qingning it was promoted.

units.zh: 有威塞軍、古可敦城、大同川、天安軍、永濟柵、安樂戍、拂雲堆。
units.en: It has Weisai Army, ancient Khotan city, the Datong River valley, Tian'an Army, Yongji Palisade, Anle garrison, and Fuyun Mound.
units.literal: There are Weisai Army, ancient Khotan city, Datong River valley, Tian'an Army, Yongji Palisade, Anle garrison, and Fuyun Mound.

units.en: Its military affairs came under the Southwest Pacification Office.
units.literal: Military affairs belonged to the Southwest Pacification Office.

units.en: It administered two counties: Rourou County.
units.literal: It governed two counties: Rourou County.

units.en: Ningren County.
units.literal: Ningren County.

units.en: Tiande Army was originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.
units.literal: Tiande Army—originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.

units.zh: 唐開元中廢橫塞軍，置天安軍於大同川。
units.en: Under Tang Kaiyuan Hengsai Army was abolished and Tian'an Army established in the Datong River valley.
units.literal: Tang Kaiyuan abolished Hengsai Army and placed Tian'an Army in the Datong River valley.

units.zh: 乾元中改天德軍，移永濟柵，今治是也。
units.en: In the Qianyuan period it became Tiande Army and shifted to Yongji Palisade—the present headquarters.
units.literal: Qianyuan era changed it to Tiande Army and moved to Yongji Palisade; the present seat is this.

units.zh: 太祖平党項，遂破天德，盡掠吏民以東。
units.en: After pacifying the Tangut the Taizu stormed Tiande and deported every official and commoner eastward.
units.literal: The Taizu pacified the Tangut and then broke Tiande, carrying off all officials and people east.

units.zh: 後置招討司，漸成井邑，乃以國族為天德軍節度使。
units.en: A pacification office followed; as settlement grew a clansman was appointed Tiande Army military commissioner.
units.literal: Later a pacification office was placed; gradually it became a settled town, and a member of the imperial clan was made Tiande Army military commissioner.

units.zh: 有黃河、黑山峪、盧城、威塞軍、秦長城、唐長城；
units.en: It has the Yellow River, Heishan Pass, Lucheng, Weisai Army, the Qin Great Wall, and the Tang Great Wall;
units.literal: There are the Yellow River, Heishan Pass, Lucheng, Weisai Army, Qin Great Wall, and Tang Great Wall;

units.zh: 又有牟那山，鉗耳觜城在其北。
units.en: Mount Mona stands here; Qian'erzui Fort lies north of it.
units.literal: There is also Mount Mona; Qian'erzui Fort lies to its north.

units.en: Ningbian Prefecture—Zhenxi Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Ningbian Prefecture, Zhenxi Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: It was Tang's Long Fort; Liao founded the prefecture.
units.literal: Originally Tang Long Fort; Liao established it.

units.en: Its military affairs came under the Southwest Pacification Office.
units.literal: Military affairs belonged to the Southwest Pacification Office.

units.en: Fengsheng Prefecture—Wuding Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.
units.literal: Fengsheng Prefecture, Wuding Army, upper grade, military commissioner.

units.en: It was originally Tang Xin Prefecture.
units.literal: Originally Tang Xin Prefecture.

units.zh: 後唐置團練使，總山後八軍，莊宗以弟存矩為之。
units.en: Later Tang placed a training commissioner over the eight mountain-rear armies; Zhuangzong gave the post to his brother Cunju.
units.literal: Later Tang set a training commissioner commanding the eight mountain-rear armies; Zhuangzong appointed his brother Cunju.

units.zh: 軍亂，殺存矩於祁州，擁大將盧文進亡歸。
units.en: Troops mutinied, slew Cunju at Qizhou, and great generals escorted Lu Wenjin in flight to surrender.
units.literal: The army mutinied, killed Cunju at Qizhou, and the great generals led Lu Wenjin to flee and submit.

units.zh: 太祖克新州，莊宗遣李嗣源復取之。
units.en: The Taizu seized Xin Prefecture; Zhuangzong dispatched Li Siyuan to retake it.
units.literal: The Taizu took Xin Prefecture; Zhuangzong sent Li Siyuan to recover it.

units.en: Tongguang year 2 promoted it to Weisai Army.
units.literal: Tongguang year 2 raised Weisai Army.

units.zh: 石晉高祖割獻，太宗改升。
units.en: Later Jin Gaozu ceded the region; Liao Emperor Taizong elevated it.
units.literal: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it in tribute; Emperor Taizong raised its rank.

units.zh: 有兩河會、溫泉、龍門山、涿鹿山。
units.en: It has the Lianghe Confluence, hot springs, Longmen Mountain, and Zhuolu Mountain.
units.literal: There are Lianghe Confluence, hot springs, Longmen Mountain, and Zhuolu Mountain.

units.zh: 東南至南京三百里，西北至西京四百四十里。
units.en: It lay three hundred li southeast of Nanjing and four hundred forty li northwest of Western Capital.
units.literal: Three hundred li southeast to Nanjing; four hundred forty li northwest to Western Capital.

units.en: Its military affairs came under the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.
units.literal: Military affairs belonged to the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.

units.en: It administered three sub-prefectures and four counties: Yongxing County.
units.literal: It governed three prefectures and four counties: Yongxing County.

units.en: It was originally Han Zhuolu County.
units.literal: Originally Han Zhuolu County land.

units.en: Here the Yellow Emperor battled Chiyou.
units.literal: The Yellow Emperor fought Chiyou here.

units.en: Eight thousand registered households.
units.literal: Eight thousand households.

units.en: Fanshan County.
units.literal: Fanshan County.

units.en: It was originally Han Jundu County.
units.literal: Originally Han Jundu County.

units.en: White-green alum comes from the mountain, giving the county its name.
units.literal: The mountain yields white-green alum, hence the name.

units.en: It has Fanshan and the Sanggan River.
units.literal: There are Fanshan and the Sanggan River.

units.en: It stood sixty li south of the prefecture.
units.literal: Sixty li south of the prefecture.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Longmen County.
units.literal: Longmen County.

units.zh: 有龍門山，石壁對峙，高數百尺，望之若門。
units.en: Longmen Mountain rises here: opposing cliffs hundreds of feet high that from a distance resemble a gate.
units.literal: There is Longmen Mountain—cliff faces cliff, several hundred feet high, looking from afar like a gate.

units.zh: 僥外諸河及沙漠潦水，皆於此趣海。
units.en: Outlying rivers and desert runoff all converge here on their way to the sea.
units.literal: Peripheral rivers and desert floodwaters all pass here toward the sea.

units.zh: 雨則俄頃水逾十仞，睛則清淺可涉，實塞北控扼之沖要也。
units.en: Rain can raise the water ten ren in moments; in fair weather it is shallow enough to wade—a critical northern frontier pass.
units.literal: When it rains water in a moment exceeds ten ren; when clear it is shallow enough to ford—a truly vital choke point controlling the northern frontier.

units.zh: 在州東北二百八十里，戶四千。
units.en: It lay two hundred eighty li northeast of the prefecture with four thousand households.
units.literal: Two hundred eighty li northeast of the prefecture; four thousand households.

units.en: Wangyun County.
units.literal: Wangyun County.

units.en: It was originally the Wangyun River valley.
units.literal: Originally Wangyun River valley land.

units.zh: 景宗於此建潛邸，因而成井肆。
units.en: Emperor Jingzong established a concealed residence here, and a market town grew up around it.
units.literal: Emperor Jingzong built a hidden residence here; thus a market town formed.

units.zh: 穆宗崩，景宗入紹國統，號禦莊。
units.en: After Emperor Muzong's death, Jingzong left this residence to inherit the imperial succession, and it became known as the imperial estate.
units.literal: When Emperor Muzong died, Jingzong left this residence to succeed to the imperial line, and the residence was called the imperial estate.

units.zh: 後置望雲縣，直隸彰湣宮，附庸於此。
units.en: Later Wangyun County was created, reporting directly to Zhangmin Palace as a dependency of this prefecture.
units.literal: Later Wangyun County was established, directly subordinate to Zhangmin Palace and attached here as a dependency.

units.en: It stood two hundred sixty li northeast of the prefecture.
units.literal: Two hundred sixty li northeast of the prefecture.

units.en: One thousand registered households.
units.literal: One thousand households.

units.en: Guihua Prefecture—Xiongwu Army, upper grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Guihua Prefecture, Xiongwu Army, upper grade, cishi.

units.en: It was originally Han Xialuo County.
units.literal: Originally Han Xialuo County.

units.en: Northern Wei renamed it Wende County.
units.literal: Northern Wei changed it to Wende County.

units.en: Tang promoted it to Wu Prefecture; Emperor Xizong renamed it Yi Prefecture.
units.literal: Tang raised it to Wu Prefecture; Emperor Xizong changed it to Yi Prefecture.

units.zh: 後唐太祖復武州，明宗又為毅州，潞王仍為武州。
units.en: Later Tang's Taizu restored Wu Prefecture; Mingzong made it Yi again; Emperor Lu returned it to Wu Prefecture.
units.literal: Later Tang Taizu restored Wu Prefecture; Emperor Mingzong again made it Yi Prefecture; Emperor Lu restored Wu Prefecture.

units.zh: 晉高祖割獻於遼，改今名。
units.en: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it to Liao and the present name was given.
units.literal: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it to Liao; the present name was adopted.

units.en: It has the Sanggan River;
units.literal: There is the Sanggan River;

units.en: the Huihe River valley;
units.literal: Huihe River valley;

units.en: the Aiyang River valley;
units.literal: Aiyang River valley;

units.en: Mount Tanshan, also known as the pass head.
units.literal: Mount Tanshan, also called the pass head.

units.zh: 有涼殿，承天皇后納涼於此，山東北三十里有新涼殿，景宗納涼於此，唯松棚數陘而已。
units.en: A Cool Hall stands where Empress Chengtian summered; thirty li northeast is New Cool Hall where Emperor Jingzong summered—nothing but pine shelters over several passes.
units.literal: There is a Cool Hall where Empress Chengtian took the cool; thirty li northeast of the mountain is New Cool Hall where Emperor Jingzong took the cool—only pine arbors over several passes.

units.en: Duanyun Ridge is sheer and lofty, giving it its name.
units.literal: Duanyun Ridge—extremely high and steep, hence the name.

units.zh: 州西北至西京四百五十里，統縣一：文德縣。
units.en: It stood four hundred fifty li northwest of Western Capital and governed one county: Wende County.
units.literal: Four hundred fifty li northwest to Western Capital; it governed one county: Wende County.

units.en: It was originally Han Nuqi County.
units.literal: Originally Han Nuqi County land.

units.en: Northern Wei founded it with ten thousand households.
units.literal: Northern Wei established it; ten thousand households.

units.en: Kehan Prefecture—Qingping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Kehan Prefecture, Qingping Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: It was Han Pan County, abolished under Northern Wei.
units.literal: Originally Han Pan County; abolished under Northern Wei.

units.zh: 北齊置北燕郡，改懷戎縣。
units.en: Northern Qi created Northern Yan Commandery and renamed it Huairou County.
units.literal: Northern Qi set Northern Yan Commandery and changed it to Huairou County.

units.en: Sui abolished the commandery and placed it in Zhuo Commandery.
units.literal: Sui abolished the commandery; it belonged to Zhuo Commandery.

units.zh: 唐武德中復置北燕州，縣仍舊。
units.en: Tang's Wude period restored Northern Yan Prefecture; the county kept its old name.
units.literal: Tang Wude era restored Northern Yan Prefecture; the county remained as before.

units.en: Zhenguan year 8 it became Gui Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhenguan year 8 changed it to Gui Prefecture.

units.zh: 五代時，奚王去諸以數千帳徙媯州，自別為西奚，號可汗州；
units.en: In the Five Dynasties Xi king Quzhu migrated several thousand households to Gui Prefecture, split off as Western Xi, and styled the seat Kehan Prefecture;
units.literal: In the Five Dynasties the Xi king Quzhu moved several thousand tents to Gui Prefecture and set himself apart as Western Xi, styled Kehan Prefecture;

units.en: The Taizu adopted the arrangement.
units.literal: The Taizu followed this arrangement.

units.zh: 有媯泉在城中，相傳舜嬪二女於此。
units.en: Gui Spring flows within the walls; tradition holds that Shun wed his two daughters here.
units.literal: There is Gui Spring in the city; tradition says Shun married his two daughters here.

units.zh: 又有溫泉、版泉、磨笄山、雞鳴山、喬山、歷山。
units.en: It also has hot springs, Ban Spring, Mojishan Mountain, Jiming Mountain, Qiao Mountain, and Li Mountain.
units.literal: There are also hot springs, Ban Spring, Mojishan Mountain, Jiming Mountain, Qiao Mountain, and Li Mountain.

units.en: The prefecture administered a single county, Huailai.
units.literal: It governed one county: Huailai County.

units.en: It was Huairou County until the Taizu renamed it.
units.literal: Originally Huairou County; the Taizu changed the name.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Ru Prefecture—Jinyang Army, middle grade, with a prefect.
units.literal: Ru Prefecture, Jinyang Army, middle grade, cishi.

units.en: Tang founded it.
units.literal: Tang established it.

units.en: Later Tang Tongguang year 2 placed it under Xin Prefecture.
units.literal: Later Tang Tongguang year 2 subordinated it to Xin Prefecture.

units.en: Emperor Taizong made it Fengsheng Prefecture while keeping it under that command.
units.literal: Emperor Taizong changed it to Fengsheng Prefecture; it still belonged there.

units.zh: 有南溪河、沽河、宋王峪、桃峪口。
units.en: It has Nanxi River, Gu River, Songwang Pass, and Taoyukou Pass.
units.literal: There are Nanxi River, Gu River, Songwang Pass, and Taoyukou Pass.

units.en: The prefecture administered a single county, Jinshan.
units.literal: It governed one county: Jinshan County.

units.en: It was originally Han Guangmi County.
units.literal: Originally Han Guangmi County land.

units.en: Tang's Tianbao period carved it from Guichuan County.
units.literal: Tang Tianbao era cut off Guichuan County and established this.

units.en: Five thousand registered households.
units.literal: Five thousand households.

units.en: Ding'an County.
units.literal: Ding'an County.

units.en: It was Han Dong'anyang County, long since abandoned.
units.literal: Originally Han Dong'anyang County land; long abolished.

units.zh: 後唐太祖伐劉仁恭，次蔚州，晨霧晦冥，占，不利深入，會雷電大作，燕軍解去，即此。
units.en: Later Tang's Taizu, attacking Liu Rengong, camped at Yu Prefecture; thick morning fog made omens unfavorable for a deep advance; thunder and lightning broke and the Yan army withdrew—here.
units.literal: Later Tang Taizu campaigning against Liu Rengong halted at Yu Prefecture; morning fog was dark; divination was unfavorable for advancing deep; thunder and lightning burst forth and the Yan army dispersed—this was the place.

units.en: Liao created Ding'an County.
units.literal: Liao established Ding'an County.

units.en: It lay sixty li northwest of the prefecture.
units.literal: Sixty li northwest to the prefecture.

units.en: Ten thousand registered households.
units.literal: Ten thousand households.

units.en: Feihu County.
units.literal: Feihu County.

units.zh: 後周大象二年置廣昌縣於五龍城，即此。
units.en: Later Zhou year 2 of Elephant established Guangchang County at Wulong Fort—here.
units.literal: Later Zhou Elephant year 2 established Guangchang County at Wulong Fort—this was the place.

units.en: In the first year of Sui Renshou it was renamed Feihu.
units.literal: In the first year of Sui Renshou renamed it Feihu.

units.zh: 相傳有狐於紫荊嶺食五粒松子，成飛仙，故云。
units.en: Legend holds that a fox on Zijing Ridge ate five pine nuts and ascended as an immortal, giving the county its name.
units.literal: Tradition says a fox on Zijing Ridge ate five pine nuts and became an immortal in flight, hence the name.

units.en: It stood one hundred forty li northwest of the prefecture.
units.literal: One hundred forty li northwest to the prefecture.

units.en: Five thousand registered households.
units.literal: Five thousand households.

units.en: Lingqiu County.
units.literal: Lingqiu County.

units.en: Han founded it.
units.literal: Han established it.

units.en: Later Han removed it.
units.literal: Later Han abolished it.

units.en: Eastern Wei re-established it under Lingqiu Commandery.
units.literal: Eastern Wei restored it, belonging to Lingqiu Commandery.

units.en: Sui Kaihuang abolished the commandery and brought it under the prefecture.
units.literal: Sui Kaihuang abolished the commandery and it came under direct rule.

units.en: Early Daye it was reassigned to Dai Prefecture.
units.literal: Early Daye it was changed to subordinate to Dai Prefecture.

units.en: Tang Wude year 6 returned it to the former status.
units.literal: Tang Wude year 6 restored the old arrangement.

units.en: It lay one hundred eighty li northeast of the prefecture.
units.literal: One hundred eighty li northeast to the prefecture.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.en: Guangling County.
units.literal: Guangling County.

units.en: It was originally Han Yanling County.
units.literal: Originally Han Yanling County.

units.en: Northern Wei Emperor Xiaowen first set Shuo Prefecture at old Dingxiang city, three hundred eighty li north of the present seat.

units.literal: Ge Rong's rebellion; abolished.

units.en: Northern Qi Tianbao year 6 restored it at a new city forty-seven li south of the present seat.
units.literal: Northern Qi Tianbao year 6 restored it at the new city forty-seven li south of the present prefecture.

units.en: Year 8 it moved to Mayi—the present walled city.
units.literal: Year 8 moved to Mayi—the present city.

units.en: Emperor Wucheng established a Northern Circuit provisional office.
units.literal: Emperor Wucheng set a Northern Circuit provisional office.

units.literal: Emperor Wudi set the Shuo Prefecture grand commandant headquarters.

units.literal: Tang Kaiyuan year 5 split off Datong Army thirty li east of Zhaoyang County; the county was established attached to the prefectural seat.

units.en: It lay forty li south of Shuo Prefecture.
units.literal: Forty li south to Shuo Prefecture.

units.en: Three thousand registered households.
units.literal: Three thousand households.

units.literal: Wu Prefecture, Xuanwei Army, lower grade, cishi.

units.en: Wei created Shenwu County.

units.zh: 唐末置武州，後唐改毅州。
units.en: Late Tang founded Wu Prefecture; Later Tang renamed it Yi Prefecture.
units.literal: Late Tang established Wu Prefecture; Later Tang changed it to Yi Prefecture.

units.zh: 重熙九年復武州，號宣威軍。

units.en: Five thousand registered households.

units.literal: Sui Kaihuang year 7 established Sheng Prefecture.

units.en: Daye year 5 it became Yulin Commandery.
units.literal: Daye year 5 changed it to Yulin Commandery.

units.zh: 唐貞觀五年於南河地置決勝州，故謂此為東勝州。
units.en: Tang Zhenguan year 5 set up Juesheng Prefecture on the south-bank lands, so this was called Eastern Sheng Prefecture.
units.literal: Tang Zhenguan year 5 established Juesheng Prefecture on the south-bank lands, hence this was called Eastern Sheng Prefecture.

units.en: Tianbao year 7 it again became Yulin Commandery.
units.literal: Tianbao year 7 it again became Yulin Commandery.

units.en: Qianyuan year 1 it was restored as Sheng Prefecture.
units.literal: Qianyuan year 1 restored it as Sheng Prefecture.

units.literal: In the first year of Shence under Emperor Taizu, he defeated the Zhenwu Army; the people of Sheng Prefecture all fled to Hedong, and the prefecture was abolished.

units.literal: Jin ceded the Dai north as tribute and it was restored.

units.en: Three hundred Yan households and one thousand frontier garrison troops were settled there.
